types.description: Abstract environment base. Not authored directly: an `environment.base` node fails to load (ERR_ABSTRACT_SUBTYPE_AUTHORED).
A named environment that stays up: production, staging. Deployments name it with @environment; a settings vault maps its secrets to it by the same name.
types.whenToUse: Every environment that exists whether or not anyone is working on it.

types.description: An environment created for one change and removed after it: a pull-request preview.

types.whenToUse: The settings and resources a project needs to run on a workstation.

types.description: Abstract build base: the attributes every build.* shares. A build is a child of an app and says how its deployable is made, the same in every environment. Not authored directly: a `build.base` node fails to load (ERR_ABSTRACT_SUBTYPE_AUTHORED).

children.name: watchExclude
children.description: Repository path globs whose change must not start a new build (`docs/**`, `*.md`). A platform that has no place for them in its own file gets them as a fact to set by hand, which its generator lists.

types.description: The app is built as a container image from a Dockerfile.
types.whenToUse: Any app whose image is described by a Dockerfile in the repository.

children.name: path
children.description: The Dockerfile's path from the repository root. Absent means `Dockerfile`.

children.name: context
children.description: The build context directory from the repository root. Absent means the root.

types.description: The app is built by a command the platform's own builder runs, with no Dockerfile.
types.whenToUse: A buildpack-style build: `npm run build`, `./gradlew bootJar`.

children.name: command
children.description: The build command, run from the repository root.

types.description: The app is a directory of files served as they are, optionally produced by a command first.
types.whenToUse: A static site or a single-page client served by a CDN.

children.name: directory
children.description: The directory of files to serve, from the repository root (`dist`).

children.name: command
children.description: The command that produces the directory. Absent means the directory is committed as it is.

types.description: How one of an app's processes runs, the same in every environment: its start command, port, health check, shutdown drain and restart policy. A platform generator writes what its platform's file can hold and lists the rest.
types.whenToUse: Every app that runs as a process. A second runtime.process is a second process of the same app (a worker beside the web server).

children.name: command
children.description: The start command. Absent means the image's or the builder's default.

children.name: port
children.description: The port the process listens on.

children.name: healthPath
children.description: The HTTP path that answers 2xx when the process is ready (`/health`).

children.name: healthTimeoutSeconds
children.description: How long a new deployment may take to pass its health check before it is failed.

children.name: drainSeconds
children.description: How long the old process keeps running after the new one is healthy, so requests in flight finish.

children.name: restart
children.description: When the platform restarts the process after it exits: always, onFailure (a non-zero exit) or never.

types.description: Abstract deployment base: an app placed in an environment on a platform. A platform pack registers the concrete subtype (`deployment.<platform>`), which takes these attributes and adds the platform's own. A deployment holds only what differs per environment; what is true everywhere sits under the app. An estate repository adds deployments the app never declared and overrides the ones it did by overlay. Not authored directly: a `deployment.base` node fails to load (ERR_ABSTRACT_SUBTYPE_AUTHORED).

children.name: app
children.description: The app deployed: `System.app` (`Shop.web`), or `pkg::System.app` from another package. It must resolve to an app.* node (ERR_DELIVERY_UNRESOLVED_REF).

children.name: environment
children.description: The environment.* node it deploys to, by name (or `pkg::name`). It must resolve (ERR_DELIVERY_UNRESOLVED_REF).

children.name: domains
children.description: The public host names that route to the app here.

children.name: replicas
children.description: How many copies run. Absent means the platform's default.

children.name: region
children.description: The platform's region name.

children.name: branch
children.description: The repository branch whose pushes deploy here.

children.name: secrets
children.description: The vault the deployment's secret settings come from, by name (a vault.* of the config pack). Recorded by name only: this pack does not require the config pack.

types.description: Abstract value base: how one setting gets its value in one deployment. A child of a deployment. A secret needs no value node: the setting is marked secret and the deployment names its vault. Not authored directly: a `value.base` node fails to load (ERR_ABSTRACT_SUBTYPE_AUTHORED).

children.name: setting
children.description: The setting this value is for, as `Group.field` (a field of an object.settings of the config pack). Recorded by name only: this pack does not require the config pack.

types.description: The setting takes a fixed value in this deployment.
types.whenToUse: A non-secret value that differs per environment: a profile name, a feature flag, a log level.

children.name: literal
children.description: The value, as a string (the setting's type parses it). Named @literal because `value` is a reserved structural key.

types.description: The setting takes a value another node produces at deploy time: a database's connection URL, another app's private address. This is how an address stays out of a repository: it is named, never written.
types.whenToUse: A setting whose value only the platform knows once the resource or app exists.

children.name: from
children.description: The node that produces the value: a resource.* or app.*, as `System.child` (`Shop.db`, or `pkg::System.child`). It must resolve (ERR_DELIVERY_UNRESOLVED_REF).

children.name: output
children.description: Which of its values: url, host, port, user, password, privateUrl, publicUrl. A platform generator maps the name to the platform's own reference and refuses one it cannot supply.
